Hands-on material is intentionally reserved for the author. This guide is not
part of the rendered book; `_quarto.yml` defines the reader-facing manuscript.

## What the volume provides

The book connects a health question with the observation structure, statistical
method, assumptions, interpretation, and reporting. It teaches basic independent
and paired analyses, with estimates and uncertainty at the centre of the result.
It includes 16 chapters, five part introductions, four content appendices,
references, worked illustrations, review questions and answers, and five figures.

| Chapter | File | Defined scope |
|:--------|:-----|:--------------|
| 1. Role of statistics | `role.qmd` | Question, population, estimand, design, unit, variable type, and workflow |
| 2. Getting started | `getting-started.qmd` | Interface orientation, import, analysis workspace, saving, and reproducibility |
| 3. Data entry and validation | `data-management.qmd` | Measurement plan, row keys, dictionary, variable properties, entry checks, and import audit |
| 4. Data cleaning and missing values | `data-cleaning.qmd` | Supported corrections, duplicates, category mapping, missingness, complete cases, and change log |
| 5. Transformations and derived variables | `data-transformation.qmd` | Units, ratios, change, recoding, reversal, scores, logs, standardisation, and verification |
| 6. Preparation for a specific analysis | `analysis-preparation.qmd` | Analysis specification, eligibility, filters, required variables, pairing, denominators, and saved record |
| 7. Descriptive statistics | `descriptive-statistics.qmd` | Counts, proportions, centre, spread, distribution, and appropriate tables |
| 8. Graphical presentation | `graphical-presentation.qmd` | Graph choice, distributions, relationships, uncertainty, and presentation |
| 9. Hypothesis-testing concepts | `hypothesis-testing-concepts.qmd` | Sampling distributions, SE, CI, hypotheses, p-values, errors, power, and multiplicity |
| 10. Two-group and paired comparisons | `comparing-two-means.qmd` | Welch, pooled and paired t procedures; rank alternatives; reasoning record and interpretation |
| 11. More than two groups | `comparing-more-than-two-means.qmd` | One-way and Welch ANOVA, contrasts, post-hoc choices, and Kruskal-Wallis |
| 12. Categorical associations | `categorical-variables.qmd` | Denominators, chi-square, Fisher, differences and ratios, and paired binary data |
| 13. Correlation | `correlation.qmd` | Linear and monotonic association, uncertainty, plots, and interpretation limits |
| 14. Simple linear regression | `linear-regression.qmd` | One predictor, slope, residuals, uncertainty, fit, and prediction limits |
| 15. Introductory logistic regression | `logistic-regression.qmd` | Binary outcomes, one predictor, odds, OR, probabilities, coding, and model limits |
| 16. Reporting results | `reporting-results.qmd` | Methods and results paragraphs, tables, figures, uncertainty, and reproducibility |

The four preparation chapters implement the agreed sequence as core content,
with each stage having its own teaching text, examples, questions, and Hands-on
space. The established `data-management.qmd` path remains in use for Chapter 3;
its broader introductory material has been developed across Chapters 3-6.

The appendices provide formulas with their conditions, a method-selection guide,
a glossary, and ten integrated conceptual practice cases with answers. The
practice appendix describes future dataset structures but supplies no raw data.

## What is to be added

Each main chapter has a separate Hands-on heading and an empty note callout;
the practice appendix has an additional box. The 17 boxes are reserved for the
author's datasets, dictionaries, saved `.omv` analyses, screenshots, procedures,
and practical interpretation. The teaching manuscript is supplied for review.
No printed result is claimed to come from an included clinical dataset.

## How it is provided

The source is an editable Quarto book in an RStudio project, with HTML and PDF
review outputs. BibTeX records support numeric references. R companion scripts
reproduce figures and calculations; their execution status is documented in
`PROJECT_REVIEW.md`. Independent Python checks verify the supplied arithmetic.

The repeated learning sequence is question, design, data, method, assumptions,
output, clinical meaning, and reporting. Dataset-specific demonstrations are
reserved for the Hands-on boxes so they can use verified software output.

## Boundary with later volumes

Simple regression illustrates an unadjusted relationship. The logistic chapter
introduces binary-outcome interpretation rather than full adjusted model building.
Neither chapter establishes causality or a validated clinical prediction tool.
Multiple-predictor models, specialist diagnostic and measurement methods,
extensive repeated measures, and survival remain planned for Volume II.
Advanced validation, causal analysis, longitudinal extensions, evidence synthesis,
and deeper jamovi-R integration remain planned for Volume III.
